[137] [[Tafsir Majma' al-Bayan: 10/333.]]

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

﴿Has there come to you the report of the Overwhelming?﴾ That is, the Resurrection, which overwhelms everything; this is the view of most exegetes.

Sa'id ibn Jubayr and Muhammad ibn Ka'b said: "al-Ghashiyah" is the Fire. Their evidence is the Almighty's saying: ﴿And the Fire will cover their faces...﴾

﴿Faces, that Day,﴾ that is, the Day of Resurrection. It was said: ﴿in humiliation﴾, abased. ﴿Labouring, toiling,﴾ some said: that is, labouring in the Fire and toiling therein. Al-Hasan and Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: they did not work for Allah in the world, so they are made to labour and toil in the Fire, struggling with chains and shackles. This is also the narration of al-Awfi from Ibn Abbas. Qatadah said: they were disdainful of obedience in the world, so they are made to labour and toil in the Fire.

Al-Kalbi said: they are dragged on their faces in the Fire. Al-Dahhak said: they are commanded to climb a mountain of iron in the Fire. And al-Nasb means persistent labour.

Ikrimah and al-Suddi said: "labouring" in the world through sins, "toiling" in the Fire on the Day of Resurrection. Sa'id ibn Jubayr and Zayd ibn Aslam said: they are the monks and the dwellers of the hermitages. This is also the narration of Abu al-Duha from Ibn Abbas.

﴿Burning in a scorching Fire.﴾ Ibn Mas'ud said: they wade through the Fire as camels wade through mud.

The common reading is with a fatha on the ta'. Abu 'Amr, Ya'qub and Abu Bakr read it with a damma (tusla), in consideration of His saying: ﴿They will be given to drink from a boiling spring (ʿayn āniyah)﴾. Qatadah said: its cooking has been going on since Allah created the heavens and the earth.

﴿They will have no food except from *darii'*﴾. Muhammad, Ikrimah and Qatadah said: it is a thorny plant lying flat on the ground, which the people of the East call "firsh al-sharq"; when it dries out, they call it *al-darii'*, and it is the most wretched and foul food. This is also the narration of al-Awfi from Ibn Abbas. Al-Wali said from him: it is a tree of fire. Ibn Zayd said: in this world, *al-darii'* is dry thorn that has no leaves, which the Arabs call *al-darii'*; but in the Hereafter it is thorn of fire.

Al-Kalbi said: no animal approaches it when it dries, and nothing grazes on it. Sa'id ibn Jubayr said it is stones. Ata' related from Ibn Abbas: it is something cast up by the salt sea, which the people of Yemen call *al-darii'*.

It has been narrated from Ibn Abbas, from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), that he said: "*al-Darii'* is something in the Fire, resembling thorns, more bitter than aloes, more foul than carrion, and hotter than the Fire." [138] [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 20/30.]] The Prophet named it *darii'*. 

'Amr ibn 'Ubayd said: al-Hasan said nothing about *al-darii'* except that it is part of the punishment that Allah has concealed. Ibn Kaysan said: it is a food by which they become humbled and abased and beseech Allah, and according to this interpretation the meaning is "that which humbles" (al-mudarri').

Abu al-Darda' and al-Hasan said: Allah will disfigure the faces of the people of the Fire on the Day of Resurrection, making them resemble their evil deeds in the world, and He will beautify the faces of the people of Paradise, making them resemble their good deeds in the world. Allah will send hunger upon the people of the Fire until what they suffer is made light in comparison; they will call for help and be given *al-darii'*, and they will call for help and be given food of choking throat, recalling that they used to swallow morsels of choking food in the world with water; so they will ask for drink because of their thirst for a thousand years, and they will be given to drink from a boiling spring, neither wholesome nor pleasant. Whenever they bring it near their faces, it strips off the skin of their faces and roasts it; when it reaches their bellies, it cuts them up. This is His saying: ﴿And they are given boiling water to drink, and it cuts their bowels to pieces.﴾

The exegetes said: When this verse was revealed, the polytheists said: "Our camels will grow fat on *al-darii'*!" So Allah revealed: ﴿It neither fattens nor satisfies hunger.﴾ And it is said: camels graze on it while it is fresh; when it dries, nothing eats it, and its fresh form is called *al-shibraq*, not *al-darii'*.

﴿Faces, that Day, joyful,﴾ pleased with their striving in the world; ﴿well-pleased in the Hereafter,﴾ when they are given Paradise in return for their deeds, and rewarded for the reward of their striving in the Hereafter, well-pleased. ﴿In a lofty Garden,﴾ ﴿where they hear no idle talk.﴾ Idle talk is futility and falsehood; it was also said: a false oath. ﴿Therein is a flowing spring,﴾ ﴿therein are raised couches,﴾ ﴿and cups set out,﴾ ﴿and cushions arranged,﴾ ﴿and carpets spread out.﴾ *Namariq* means cushions, pillows and armrests set in rows, placed side by side; its singular is *namraqah*. The poet said:

*Elders and youths, handsome of face,*
*upon arranged couches and cushions.* [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 20/34.]]

﴿Zarabi (carpets)﴾ means broad rugs. Ibn Abbas said: they are fine cloths with a soft nap; the singular is *zaribah*. ﴿Spread out (mabthuthah)﴾: spread wide; it was also said: scattered throughout the gatherings.

﴿Will they not look...﴾ — the exegetes said: when Allah described what is in Paradise in this surah, the people of disbelief and error were astonished and denied it, so Allah reminded them of His creation, saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿Will they not look at the camels, how they were created?﴾

The camel was among the sustenance of the Arabs and those around them. The wise have spoken regarding why Allah singled out the camel from among all animals. Muqatil said: because they had never seen a beast greater than it, and few of them had seen the elephant. Al-Kalbi said: because it rises with its load while kneeling, and no other animal does so; nor is any animal as easy to lead or drive as it. Qatadah said: Allah mentioned the elevation of the couches of Paradise and their carpets, so they said: "How shall we ascend?" So Allah revealed this verse.

Al-Hasan was asked about this verse, and it was said to him: "Is the elephant not greater as a wonder?" He said: As for the elephant, the Arabs are far removed from it; moreover, it is a swine, which one does not ride, nor eat its flesh, nor milk its yield; whereas the camel is among the most precious and valued property of the Arabs.

Al-Hasan also said: they eat only the date-stone and fodder, and it yields milk. It was said: because in its size it is gentle to heavy loads and submits to a weak leader, so that a small child can take hold of its halter and lead it wherever he wishes.

Ustadh Abu al-Qasim ibn Habib related that he saw in some exegesis that a mouse took hold of a she-camel's halter and began pulling her, while the she-camel followed, until it entered the hole and pulled the halter; then the she-camel moved and pulled it back, bringing her mouth near the mouse's hole. Glory be to Him who measured it and subjected it.

Abdullah ibn Hamid informed us, saying: Ahmad ibn Abdullah informed us, saying: Muhammad ibn al-'Ala' related to us, saying:

Waki' related to us from Yunus ibn Abi Ishaq, from his father, from Shurayh, that he used to say: "Come out with us to al-Kunasah until we look at ﴿the camels, how they were created﴾."

It was said: "the camels" here means the clouds, but I have found no basis for this in the books of the imams. ﴿And at the sky, how it was raised,﴾ ﴿and at the mountains, how they were set up,﴾ ﴿and at the earth, how it was spread out (sutihat)﴾ — spread out.

Anas ibn Malik said: I prayed behind 'Ali ibn Abi Talib, and he recited ﴿Will you not look at the camels, how they were created, and so they were raised, and set up, and spread out﴾, with the ta' vowelled with a damma (on the verb "spread out": *sutihat*, with a raised ta').

And al-Hasan read *suttihat* with shaddah.

[137] [[Tafsir Majma' al-Bayan: 10/333.]]

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

﴿Has there come to you the report of the Overwhelming?﴾ That is, the Resurrection, which overwhelms everything; this is the view of most exegetes.

Sa'id ibn Jubayr and Muhammad ibn Ka'b said: "al-Ghashiyah" is the Fire. Their evidence is the Almighty's saying: ﴿And the Fire will cover their faces...﴾

﴿Faces, that Day,﴾ that is, the Day of Resurrection. It was said: ﴿in humiliation﴾, abased. ﴿Labouring, toiling,﴾ some said: that is, labouring in the Fire and toiling therein. Al-Hasan and Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: they did not work for Allah in the world, so they are made to labour and toil in the Fire, struggling with chains and shackles. This is also the narration of al-Awfi from Ibn Abbas. Qatadah said: they were disdainful of obedience in the world, so they are made to labour and toil in the Fire.

Al-Kalbi said: they are dragged on their faces in the Fire. Al-Dahhak said: they are commanded to climb a mountain of iron in the Fire. And al-Nasb means persistent labour.

Ikrimah and al-Suddi said: "labouring" in the world through sins, "toiling" in the Fire on the Day of Resurrection. Sa'id ibn Jubayr and Zayd ibn Aslam said: they are the monks and the dwellers of the hermitages. This is also the narration of Abu al-Duha from Ibn Abbas.

﴿Burning in a scorching Fire.﴾ Ibn Mas'ud said: they wade through the Fire as camels wade through mud.

The common reading is with a fatha on the ta'. Abu 'Amr, Ya'qub and Abu Bakr read it with a damma (tusla), in consideration of His saying: ﴿They will be given to drink from a boiling spring (ʿayn āniyah)﴾. Qatadah said: its cooking has been going on since Allah created the heavens and the earth.

﴿They will have no food except from *darii'*﴾. Muhammad, Ikrimah and Qatadah said: it is a thorny plant lying flat on the ground, which the people of the East call "firsh al-sharq"; when it dries out, they call it *al-darii'*, and it is the most wretched and foul food. This is also the narration of al-Awfi from Ibn Abbas. Al-Wali said from him: it is a tree of fire. Ibn Zayd said: in this world, *al-darii'* is dry thorn that has no leaves, which the Arabs call *al-darii'*; but in the Hereafter it is thorn of fire.

Al-Kalbi said: no animal approaches it when it dries, and nothing grazes on it. Sa'id ibn Jubayr said it is stones. Ata' related from Ibn Abbas: it is something cast up by the salt sea, which the people of Yemen call *al-darii'*.

It has been narrated from Ibn Abbas, from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), that he said: "*al-Darii'* is something in the Fire, resembling thorns, more bitter than aloes, more foul than carrion, and hotter than the Fire." [138] [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 20/30.]] The Prophet named it *darii'*. 

'Amr ibn 'Ubayd said: al-Hasan said nothing about *al-darii'* except that it is part of the punishment that Allah has concealed. Ibn Kaysan said: it is a food by which they become humbled and abased and beseech Allah, and according to this interpretation the meaning is "that which humbles" (al-mudarri').

Abu al-Darda' and al-Hasan said: Allah will disfigure the faces of the people of the Fire on the Day of Resurrection, making them resemble their evil deeds in the world, and He will beautify the faces of the people of Paradise, making them resemble their good deeds in the world. Allah will send hunger upon the people of the Fire until what they suffer is made light in comparison; they will call for help and be given *al-darii'*, and they will call for help and be given food of choking throat, recalling that they used to swallow morsels of choking food in the world with water; so they will ask for drink because of their thirst for a thousand years, and they will be given to drink from a boiling spring, neither wholesome nor pleasant. Whenever they bring it near their faces, it strips off the skin of their faces and roasts it; when it reaches their bellies, it cuts them up. This is His saying: ﴿And they are given boiling water to drink, and it cuts their bowels to pieces.﴾

The exegetes said: When this verse was revealed, the polytheists said: "Our camels will grow fat on *al-darii'*!" So Allah revealed: ﴿It neither fattens nor satisfies hunger.﴾ And it is said: camels graze on it while it is fresh; when it dries, nothing eats it, and its fresh form is called *al-shibraq*, not *al-darii'*.

﴿Faces, that Day, joyful,﴾ pleased with their striving in the world; ﴿well-pleased in the Hereafter,﴾ when they are given Paradise in return for their deeds, and rewarded for the reward of their striving in the Hereafter, well-pleased. ﴿In a lofty Garden,﴾ ﴿where they hear no idle talk.﴾ Idle talk is futility and falsehood; it was also said: a false oath. ﴿Therein is a flowing spring,﴾ ﴿therein are raised couches,﴾ ﴿and cups set out,﴾ ﴿and cushions arranged,﴾ ﴿and carpets spread out.﴾ *Namariq* means cushions, pillows and armrests set in rows, placed side by side; its singular is *namraqah*. The poet said:

*Elders and youths, handsome of face,*
*upon arranged couches and cushions.* [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 20/34.]]

﴿Zarabi (carpets)﴾ means broad rugs. Ibn Abbas said: they are fine cloths with a soft nap; the singular is *zaribah*. ﴿Spread out (mabthuthah)﴾: spread wide; it was also said: scattered throughout the gatherings.

﴿Will they not look...﴾ — the exegetes said: when Allah described what is in Paradise in this surah, the people of disbelief and error were astonished and denied it, so Allah reminded them of His creation, saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿Will they not look at the camels, how they were created?﴾

The camel was among the sustenance of the Arabs and those around them. The wise have spoken regarding why Allah singled out the camel from among all animals. Muqatil said: because they had never seen a beast greater than it, and few of them had seen the elephant. Al-Kalbi said: because it rises with its load while kneeling, and no other animal does so; nor is any animal as easy to lead or drive as it. Qatadah said: Allah mentioned the elevation of the couches of Paradise and their carpets, so they said: "How shall we ascend?" So Allah revealed this verse.

Al-Hasan was asked about this verse, and it was said to him: "Is the elephant not greater as a wonder?" He said: As for the elephant, the Arabs are far removed from it; moreover, it is a swine, which one does not ride, nor eat its flesh, nor milk its yield; whereas the camel is among the most precious and valued property of the Arabs.

Al-Hasan also said: they eat only the date-stone and fodder, and it yields milk. It was said: because in its size it is gentle to heavy loads and submits to a weak leader, so that a small child can take hold of its halter and lead it wherever he wishes.

Ustadh Abu al-Qasim ibn Habib related that he saw in some exegesis that a mouse took hold of a she-camel's halter and began pulling her, while the she-camel followed, until it entered the hole and pulled the halter; then the she-camel moved and pulled it back, bringing her mouth near the mouse's hole. Glory be to Him who measured it and subjected it.

Abdullah ibn Hamid informed us, saying: Ahmad ibn Abdullah informed us, saying: Muhammad ibn al-'Ala' related to us, saying:

Waki' related to us from Yunus ibn Abi Ishaq, from his father, from Shurayh, that he used to say: "Come out with us to al-Kunasah until we look at ﴿the camels, how they were created﴾."

It was said: "the camels" here means the clouds, but I have found no basis for this in the books of the imams. ﴿And at the sky, how it was raised,﴾ ﴿and at the mountains, how they were set up,﴾ ﴿and at the earth, how it was spread out (sutihat)﴾ — spread out.

Anas ibn Malik said: I prayed behind 'Ali ibn Abi Talib, and he recited ﴿Will you not look at the camels, how they were created, and so they were raised, and set up, and spread out﴾, with the ta' vowelled with a damma (on the verb "spread out": *sutihat*, with a raised ta').

And al-Hasan read *suttihat* with shaddah.

[137] [[Tafsir Majma' al-Bayan: 10/333.]]

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

﴿Has there come to you the report of the Overwhelming?﴾ That is, the Resurrection, which overwhelms everything; this is the view of most exegetes.

Sa'id ibn Jubayr and Muhammad ibn Ka'b said: "al-Ghashiyah" is the Fire. Their evidence is the Almighty's saying: ﴿And the Fire will cover their faces...﴾

﴿Faces, that Day,﴾ that is, the Day of Resurrection. It was said: ﴿in humiliation﴾, abased. ﴿Labouring, toiling,﴾ some said: that is, labouring in the Fire and toiling therein. Al-Hasan and Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: they did not work for Allah in the world, so they are made to labour and toil in the Fire, struggling with chains and shackles. This is also the narration of al-Awfi from Ibn Abbas. Qatadah said: they were disdainful of obedience in the world, so they are made to labour and toil in the Fire.

Al-Kalbi said: they are dragged on their faces in the Fire. Al-Dahhak said: they are commanded to climb a mountain of iron in the Fire. And al-Nasb means persistent labour.

Ikrimah and al-Suddi said: "labouring" in the world through sins, "toiling" in the Fire on the Day of Resurrection. Sa'id ibn Jubayr and Zayd ibn Aslam said: they are the monks and the dwellers of the hermitages. This is also the narration of Abu al-Duha from Ibn Abbas.

﴿Burning in a scorching Fire.﴾ Ibn Mas'ud said: they wade through the Fire as camels wade through mud.

The common reading is with a fatha on the ta'. Abu 'Amr, Ya'qub and Abu Bakr read it with a damma (tusla), in consideration of His saying: ﴿They will be given to drink from a boiling spring (ʿayn āniyah)﴾. Qatadah said: its cooking has been going on since Allah created the heavens and the earth.

﴿They will have no food except from *darii'*﴾. Muhammad, Ikrimah and Qatadah said: it is a thorny plant lying flat on the ground, which the people of the East call "firsh al-sharq"; when it dries out, they call it *al-darii'*, and it is the most wretched and foul food. This is also the narration of al-Awfi from Ibn Abbas. Al-Wali said from him: it is a tree of fire. Ibn Zayd said: in this world, *al-darii'* is dry thorn that has no leaves, which the Arabs call *al-darii'*; but in the Hereafter it is thorn of fire.

Al-Kalbi said: no animal approaches it when it dries, and nothing grazes on it. Sa'id ibn Jubayr said it is stones. Ata' related from Ibn Abbas: it is something cast up by the salt sea, which the people of Yemen call *al-darii'*.

It has been narrated from Ibn Abbas, from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), that he said: "*al-Darii'* is something in the Fire, resembling thorns, more bitter than aloes, more foul than carrion, and hotter than the Fire." [138] [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 20/30.]] The Prophet named it *darii'*. 

'Amr ibn 'Ubayd said: al-Hasan said nothing about *al-darii'* except that it is part of the punishment that Allah has concealed. Ibn Kaysan said: it is a food by which they become humbled and abased and beseech Allah, and according to this interpretation the meaning is "that which humbles" (al-mudarri').

Abu al-Darda' and al-Hasan said: Allah will disfigure the faces of the people of the Fire on the Day of Resurrection, making them resemble their evil deeds in the world, and He will beautify the faces of the people of Paradise, making them resemble their good deeds in the world. Allah will send hunger upon the people of the Fire until what they suffer is made light in comparison; they will call for help and be given *al-darii'*, and they will call for help and be given food of choking throat, recalling that they used to swallow morsels of choking food in the world with water; so they will ask for drink because of their thirst for a thousand years, and they will be given to drink from a boiling spring, neither wholesome nor pleasant. Whenever they bring it near their faces, it strips off the skin of their faces and roasts it; when it reaches their bellies, it cuts them up. This is His saying: ﴿And they are given boiling water to drink, and it cuts their bowels to pieces.﴾

The exegetes said: When this verse was revealed, the polytheists said: "Our camels will grow fat on *al-darii'*!" So Allah revealed: ﴿It neither fattens nor satisfies hunger.﴾ And it is said: camels graze on it while it is fresh; when it dries, nothing eats it, and its fresh form is called *al-shibraq*, not *al-darii'*.

﴿Faces, that Day, joyful,﴾ pleased with their striving in the world; ﴿well-pleased in the Hereafter,﴾ when they are given Paradise in return for their deeds, and rewarded for the reward of their striving in the Hereafter, well-pleased. ﴿In a lofty Garden,﴾ ﴿where they hear no idle talk.﴾ Idle talk is futility and falsehood; it was also said: a false oath. ﴿Therein is a flowing spring,﴾ ﴿therein are raised couches,﴾ ﴿and cups set out,﴾ ﴿and cushions arranged,﴾ ﴿and carpets spread out.﴾ *Namariq* means cushions, pillows and armrests set in rows, placed side by side; its singular is *namraqah*. The poet said:

*Elders and youths, handsome of face,*
*upon arranged couches and cushions.* [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 20/34.]]

﴿Zarabi (carpets)﴾ means broad rugs. Ibn Abbas said: they are fine cloths with a soft nap; the singular is *zaribah*. ﴿Spread out (mabthuthah)﴾: spread wide; it was also said: scattered throughout the gatherings.

﴿Will they not look...﴾ — the exegetes said: when Allah described what is in Paradise in this surah, the people of disbelief and error were astonished and denied it, so Allah reminded them of His creation, saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿Will they not look at the camels, how they were created?﴾

The camel was among the sustenance of the Arabs and those around them. The wise have spoken regarding why Allah singled out the camel from among all animals. Muqatil said: because they had never seen a beast greater than it, and few of them had seen the elephant. Al-Kalbi said: because it rises with its load while kneeling, and no other animal does so; nor is any animal as easy to lead or drive as it. Qatadah said: Allah mentioned the elevation of the couches of Paradise and their carpets, so they said: "How shall we ascend?" So Allah revealed this verse.

Al-Hasan was asked about this verse, and it was said to him: "Is the elephant not greater as a wonder?" He said: As for the elephant, the Arabs are far removed from it; moreover, it is a swine, which one does not ride, nor eat its flesh, nor milk its yield; whereas the camel is among the most precious and valued property of the Arabs.

Al-Hasan also said: they eat only the date-stone and fodder, and it yields milk. It was said: because in its size it is gentle to heavy loads and submits to a weak leader, so that a small child can take hold of its halter and lead it wherever he wishes.

Ustadh Abu al-Qasim ibn Habib related that he saw in some exegesis that a mouse took hold of a she-camel's halter and began pulling her, while the she-camel followed, until it entered the hole and pulled the halter; then the she-camel moved and pulled it back, bringing her mouth near the mouse's hole. Glory be to Him who measured it and subjected it.

Abdullah ibn Hamid informed us, saying: Ahmad ibn Abdullah informed us, saying: Muhammad ibn al-'Ala' related to us, saying:

Waki' related to us from Yunus ibn Abi Ishaq, from his father, from Shurayh, that he used to say: "Come out with us to al-Kunasah until we look at ﴿the camels, how they were created﴾."

It was said: "the camels" here means the clouds, but I have found no basis for this in the books of the imams. ﴿And at the sky, how it was raised,﴾ ﴿and at the mountains, how they were set up,﴾ ﴿and at the earth, how it was spread out (sutihat)﴾ — spread out.

Anas ibn Malik said: I prayed behind 'Ali ibn Abi Talib, and he recited ﴿Will you not look at the camels, how they were created, and so they were raised, and set up, and spread out﴾, with the ta' vowelled with a damma (on the verb "spread out": *sutihat*, with a raised ta').

And al-Hasan read *suttihat* with shaddah.

[137] [[Tafsir Majma' al-Bayan: 10/333.]]

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

﴿Has there come to you the report of the Overwhelming?﴾ That is, the Resurrection, which overwhelms everything; this is the view of most exegetes.

Sa'id ibn Jubayr and Muhammad ibn Ka'b said: "al-Ghashiyah" is the Fire. Their evidence is the Almighty's saying: ﴿And the Fire will cover their faces...﴾

﴿Faces, that Day,﴾ that is, the Day of Resurrection. It was said: ﴿in humiliation﴾, abased. ﴿Labouring, toiling,﴾ some said: that is, labouring in the Fire and toiling therein. Al-Hasan and Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: they did not work for Allah in the world, so they are made to labour and toil in the Fire, struggling with chains and shackles. This is also the narration of al-Awfi from Ibn Abbas. Qatadah said: they were disdainful of obedience in the world, so they are made to labour and toil in the Fire.

Al-Kalbi said: they are dragged on their faces in the Fire. Al-Dahhak said: they are commanded to climb a mountain of iron in the Fire. And al-Nasb means persistent labour.

Ikrimah and al-Suddi said: "labouring" in the world through sins, "toiling" in the Fire on the Day of Resurrection. Sa'id ibn Jubayr and Zayd ibn Aslam said: they are the monks and the dwellers of the hermitages. This is also the narration of Abu al-Duha from Ibn Abbas.

﴿Burning in a scorching Fire.﴾ Ibn Mas'ud said: they wade through the Fire as camels wade through mud.

The common reading is with a fatha on the ta'. Abu 'Amr, Ya'qub and Abu Bakr read it with a damma (tusla), in consideration of His saying: ﴿They will be given to drink from a boiling spring (ʿayn āniyah)﴾. Qatadah said: its cooking has been going on since Allah created the heavens and the earth.

﴿They will have no food except from *darii'*﴾. Muhammad, Ikrimah and Qatadah said: it is a thorny plant lying flat on the ground, which the people of the East call "firsh al-sharq"; when it dries out, they call it *al-darii'*, and it is the most wretched and foul food. This is also the narration of al-Awfi from Ibn Abbas. Al-Wali said from him: it is a tree of fire. Ibn Zayd said: in this world, *al-darii'* is dry thorn that has no leaves, which the Arabs call *al-darii'*; but in the Hereafter it is thorn of fire.

Al-Kalbi said: no animal approaches it when it dries, and nothing grazes on it. Sa'id ibn Jubayr said it is stones. Ata' related from Ibn Abbas: it is something cast up by the salt sea, which the people of Yemen call *al-darii'*.

It has been narrated from Ibn Abbas, from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), that he said: "*al-Darii'* is something in the Fire, resembling thorns, more bitter than aloes, more foul than carrion, and hotter than the Fire." [138] [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 20/30.]] The Prophet named it *darii'*. 

'Amr ibn 'Ubayd said: al-Hasan said nothing about *al-darii'* except that it is part of the punishment that Allah has concealed. Ibn Kaysan said: it is a food by which they become humbled and abased and beseech Allah, and according to this interpretation the meaning is "that which humbles" (al-mudarri').

Abu al-Darda' and al-Hasan said: Allah will disfigure the faces of the people of the Fire on the Day of Resurrection, making them resemble their evil deeds in the world, and He will beautify the faces of the people of Paradise, making them resemble their good deeds in the world. Allah will send hunger upon the people of the Fire until what they suffer is made light in comparison; they will call for help and be given *al-darii'*, and they will call for help and be given food of choking throat, recalling that they used to swallow morsels of choking food in the world with water; so they will ask for drink because of their thirst for a thousand years, and they will be given to drink from a boiling spring, neither wholesome nor pleasant. Whenever they bring it near their faces, it strips off the skin of their faces and roasts it; when it reaches their bellies, it cuts them up. This is His saying: ﴿And they are given boiling water to drink, and it cuts their bowels to pieces.﴾

The exegetes said: When this verse was revealed, the polytheists said: "Our camels will grow fat on *al-darii'*!" So Allah revealed: ﴿It neither fattens nor satisfies hunger.﴾ And it is said: camels graze on it while it is fresh; when it dries, nothing eats it, and its fresh form is called *al-shibraq*, not *al-darii'*.

﴿Faces, that Day, joyful,﴾ pleased with their striving in the world; ﴿well-pleased in the Hereafter,﴾ when they are given Paradise in return for their deeds, and rewarded for the reward of their striving in the Hereafter, well-pleased. ﴿In a lofty Garden,﴾ ﴿where they hear no idle talk.﴾ Idle talk is futility and falsehood; it was also said: a false oath. ﴿Therein is a flowing spring,﴾ ﴿therein are raised couches,﴾ ﴿and cups set out,﴾ ﴿and cushions arranged,﴾ ﴿and carpets spread out.﴾ *Namariq* means cushions, pillows and armrests set in rows, placed side by side; its singular is *namraqah*. The poet said:

*Elders and youths, handsome of face,*
*upon arranged couches and cushions.* [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 20/34.]]

﴿Zarabi (carpets)﴾ means broad rugs. Ibn Abbas said: they are fine cloths with a soft nap; the singular is *zaribah*. ﴿Spread out (mabthuthah)﴾: spread wide; it was also said: scattered throughout the gatherings.

﴿Will they not look...﴾ — the exegetes said: when Allah described what is in Paradise in this surah, the people of disbelief and error were astonished and denied it, so Allah reminded them of His creation, saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿Will they not look at the camels, how they were created?﴾

The camel was among the sustenance of the Arabs and those around them. The wise have spoken regarding why Allah singled out the camel from among all animals. Muqatil said: because they had never seen a beast greater than it, and few of them had seen the elephant. Al-Kalbi said: because it rises with its load while kneeling, and no other animal does so; nor is any animal as easy to lead or drive as it. Qatadah said: Allah mentioned the elevation of the couches of Paradise and their carpets, so they said: "How shall we ascend?" So Allah revealed this verse.

Al-Hasan was asked about this verse, and it was said to him: "Is the elephant not greater as a wonder?" He said: As for the elephant, the Arabs are far removed from it; moreover, it is a swine, which one does not ride, nor eat its flesh, nor milk its yield; whereas the camel is among the most precious and valued property of the Arabs.

Al-Hasan also said: they eat only the date-stone and fodder, and it yields milk. It was said: because in its size it is gentle to heavy loads and submits to a weak leader, so that a small child can take hold of its halter and lead it wherever he wishes.

Ustadh Abu al-Qasim ibn Habib related that he saw in some exegesis that a mouse took hold of a she-camel's halter and began pulling her, while the she-camel followed, until it entered the hole and pulled the halter; then the she-camel moved and pulled it back, bringing her mouth near the mouse's hole. Glory be to Him who measured it and subjected it.

Abdullah ibn Hamid informed us, saying: Ahmad ibn Abdullah informed us, saying: Muhammad ibn al-'Ala' related to us, saying:

Waki' related to us from Yunus ibn Abi Ishaq, from his father, from Shurayh, that he used to say: "Come out with us to al-Kunasah until we look at ﴿the camels, how they were created﴾."

It was said: "the camels" here means the clouds, but I have found no basis for this in the books of the imams. ﴿And at the sky, how it was raised,﴾ ﴿and at the mountains, how they were set up,﴾ ﴿and at the earth, how it was spread out (sutihat)﴾ — spread out.

Anas ibn Malik said: I prayed behind 'Ali ibn Abi Talib, and he recited ﴿Will you not look at the camels, how they were created, and so they were raised, and set up, and spread out﴾, with the ta' vowelled with a damma (on the verb "spread out": *sutihat*, with a raised ta').

And al-Hasan read *suttihat* with shaddah.

[137] [[Tafsir Majma' al-Bayan: 10/333.]]

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

﴿Has there come to you the report of the Overwhelming?﴾ That is, the Resurrection, which overwhelms everything; this is the view of most exegetes.

Sa'id ibn Jubayr and Muhammad ibn Ka'b said: "al-Ghashiyah" is the Fire. Their evidence is the Almighty's saying: ﴿And the Fire will cover their faces...﴾

﴿Faces, that Day,﴾ that is, the Day of Resurrection. It was said: ﴿in humiliation﴾, abased. ﴿Labouring, toiling,﴾ some said: that is, labouring in the Fire and toiling therein. Al-Hasan and Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: they did not work for Allah in the world, so they are made to labour and toil in the Fire, struggling with chains and shackles. This is also the narration of al-Awfi from Ibn Abbas. Qatadah said: they were disdainful of obedience in the world, so they are made to labour and toil in the Fire.

Al-Kalbi said: they are dragged on their faces in the Fire. Al-Dahhak said: they are commanded to climb a mountain of iron in the Fire. And al-Nasb means persistent labour.

Ikrimah and al-Suddi said: "labouring" in the world through sins, "toiling" in the Fire on the Day of Resurrection. Sa'id ibn Jubayr and Zayd ibn Aslam said: they are the monks and the dwellers of the hermitages. This is also the narration of Abu al-Duha from Ibn Abbas.

﴿Burning in a scorching Fire.﴾ Ibn Mas'ud said: they wade through the Fire as camels wade through mud.

The common reading is with a fatha on the ta'. Abu 'Amr, Ya'qub and Abu Bakr read it with a damma (tusla), in consideration of His saying: ﴿They will be given to drink from a boiling spring (ʿayn āniyah)﴾. Qatadah said: its cooking has been going on since Allah created the heavens and the earth.

﴿They will have no food except from *darii'*﴾. Muhammad, Ikrimah and Qatadah said: it is a thorny plant lying flat on the ground, which the people of the East call "firsh al-sharq"; when it dries out, they call it *al-darii'*, and it is the most wretched and foul food. This is also the narration of al-Awfi from Ibn Abbas. Al-Wali said from him: it is a tree of fire. Ibn Zayd said: in this world, *al-darii'* is dry thorn that has no leaves, which the Arabs call *al-darii'*; but in the Hereafter it is thorn of fire.

Al-Kalbi said: no animal approaches it when it dries, and nothing grazes on it. Sa'id ibn Jubayr said it is stones. Ata' related from Ibn Abbas: it is something cast up by the salt sea, which the people of Yemen call *al-darii'*.

It has been narrated from Ibn Abbas, from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), that he said: "*al-Darii'* is something in the Fire, resembling thorns, more bitter than aloes, more foul than carrion, and hotter than the Fire." [138] [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 20/30.]] The Prophet named it *darii'*. 

'Amr ibn 'Ubayd said: al-Hasan said nothing about *al-darii'* except that it is part of the punishment that Allah has concealed. Ibn Kaysan said: it is a food by which they become humbled and abased and beseech Allah, and according to this interpretation the meaning is "that which humbles" (al-mudarri').

Abu al-Darda' and al-Hasan said: Allah will disfigure the faces of the people of the Fire on the Day of Resurrection, making them resemble their evil deeds in the world, and He will beautify the faces of the people of Paradise, making them resemble their good deeds in the world. Allah will send hunger upon the people of the Fire until what they suffer is made light in comparison; they will call for help and be given *al-darii'*, and they will call for help and be given food of choking throat, recalling that they used to swallow morsels of choking food in the world with water; so they will ask for drink because of their thirst for a thousand years, and they will be given to drink from a boiling spring, neither wholesome nor pleasant. Whenever they bring it near their faces, it strips off the skin of their faces and roasts it; when it reaches their bellies, it cuts them up. This is His saying: ﴿And they are given boiling water to drink, and it cuts their bowels to pieces.﴾

The exegetes said: When this verse was revealed, the polytheists said: "Our camels will grow fat on *al-darii'*!" So Allah revealed: ﴿It neither fattens nor satisfies hunger.﴾ And it is said: camels graze on it while it is fresh; when it dries, nothing eats it, and its fresh form is called *al-shibraq*, not *al-darii'*.

﴿Faces, that Day, joyful,﴾ pleased with their striving in the world; ﴿well-pleased in the Hereafter,﴾ when they are given Paradise in return for their deeds, and rewarded for the reward of their striving in the Hereafter, well-pleased. ﴿In a lofty Garden,﴾ ﴿where they hear no idle talk.﴾ Idle talk is futility and falsehood; it was also said: a false oath. ﴿Therein is a flowing spring,﴾ ﴿therein are raised couches,﴾ ﴿and cups set out,﴾ ﴿and cushions arranged,﴾ ﴿and carpets spread out.﴾ *Namariq* means cushions, pillows and armrests set in rows, placed side by side; its singular is *namraqah*. The poet said:

*Elders and youths, handsome of face,*
*upon arranged couches and cushions.* [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 20/34.]]

﴿Zarabi (carpets)﴾ means broad rugs. Ibn Abbas said: they are fine cloths with a soft nap; the singular is *zaribah*. ﴿Spread out (mabthuthah)﴾: spread wide; it was also said: scattered throughout the gatherings.

﴿Will they not look...﴾ — the exegetes said: when Allah described what is in Paradise in this surah, the people of disbelief and error were astonished and denied it, so Allah reminded them of His creation, saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿Will they not look at the camels, how they were created?﴾

The camel was among the sustenance of the Arabs and those around them. The wise have spoken regarding why Allah singled out the camel from among all animals. Muqatil said: because they had never seen a beast greater than it, and few of them had seen the elephant. Al-Kalbi said: because it rises with its load while kneeling, and no other animal does so; nor is any animal as easy to lead or drive as it. Qatadah said: Allah mentioned the elevation of the couches of Paradise and their carpets, so they said: "How shall we ascend?" So Allah revealed this verse.

Al-Hasan was asked about this verse, and it was said to him: "Is the elephant not greater as a wonder?" He said: As for the elephant, the Arabs are far removed from it; moreover, it is a swine, which one does not ride, nor eat its flesh, nor milk its yield; whereas the camel is among the most precious and valued property of the Arabs.

Al-Hasan also said: they eat only the date-stone and fodder, and it yields milk. It was said: because in its size it is gentle to heavy loads and submits to a weak leader, so that a small child can take hold of its halter and lead it wherever he wishes.

Ustadh Abu al-Qasim ibn Habib related that he saw in some exegesis that a mouse took hold of a she-camel's halter and began pulling her, while the she-camel followed, until it entered the hole and pulled the halter; then the she-camel moved and pulled it back, bringing her mouth near the mouse's hole. Glory be to Him who measured it and subjected it.

Abdullah ibn Hamid informed us, saying: Ahmad ibn Abdullah informed us, saying: Muhammad ibn al-'Ala' related to us, saying:

Waki' related to us from Yunus ibn Abi Ishaq, from his father, from Shurayh, that he used to say: "Come out with us to al-Kunasah until we look at ﴿the camels, how they were created﴾."

It was said: "the camels" here means the clouds, but I have found no basis for this in the books of the imams. ﴿And at the sky, how it was raised,﴾ ﴿and at the mountains, how they were set up,﴾ ﴿and at the earth, how it was spread out (sutihat)﴾ — spread out.

Anas ibn Malik said: I prayed behind 'Ali ibn Abi Talib, and he recited ﴿Will you not look at the camels, how they were created, and so they were raised, and set up, and spread out﴾, with the ta' vowelled with a damma (on the verb "spread out": *sutihat*, with a raised ta').

And al-Hasan read *suttihat* with shaddah.

[137] [[Tafsir Majma' al-Bayan: 10/333.]]

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

﴿Has there come to you the report of the Overwhelming?﴾ That is, the Resurrection, which overwhelms everything; this is the view of most exegetes.

Sa'id ibn Jubayr and Muhammad ibn Ka'b said: "al-Ghashiyah" is the Fire. Their evidence is the Almighty's saying: ﴿And the Fire will cover their faces...﴾

﴿Faces, that Day,﴾ that is, the Day of Resurrection. It was said: ﴿in humiliation﴾, abased. ﴿Labouring, toiling,﴾ some said: that is, labouring in the Fire and toiling therein. Al-Hasan and Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: they did not work for Allah in the world, so they are made to labour and toil in the Fire, struggling with chains and shackles. This is also the narration of al-Awfi from Ibn Abbas. Qatadah said: they were disdainful of obedience in the world, so they are made to labour and toil in the Fire.

Al-Kalbi said: they are dragged on their faces in the Fire. Al-Dahhak said: they are commanded to climb a mountain of iron in the Fire. And al-Nasb means persistent labour.

Ikrimah and al-Suddi said: "labouring" in the world through sins, "toiling" in the Fire on the Day of Resurrection. Sa'id ibn Jubayr and Zayd ibn Aslam said: they are the monks and the dwellers of the hermitages. This is also the narration of Abu al-Duha from Ibn Abbas.

﴿Burning in a scorching Fire.﴾ Ibn Mas'ud said: they wade through the Fire as camels wade through mud.

The common reading is with a fatha on the ta'. Abu 'Amr, Ya'qub and Abu Bakr read it with a damma (tusla), in consideration of His saying: ﴿They will be given to drink from a boiling spring (ʿayn āniyah)﴾. Qatadah said: its cooking has been going on since Allah created the heavens and the earth.

﴿They will have no food except from *darii'*﴾. Muhammad, Ikrimah and Qatadah said: it is a thorny plant lying flat on the ground, which the people of the East call "firsh al-sharq"; when it dries out, they call it *al-darii'*, and it is the most wretched and foul food. This is also the narration of al-Awfi from Ibn Abbas. Al-Wali said from him: it is a tree of fire. Ibn Zayd said: in this world, *al-darii'* is dry thorn that has no leaves, which the Arabs call *al-darii'*; but in the Hereafter it is thorn of fire.

Al-Kalbi said: no animal approaches it when it dries, and nothing grazes on it. Sa'id ibn Jubayr said it is stones. Ata' related from Ibn Abbas: it is something cast up by the salt sea, which the people of Yemen call *al-darii'*.

It has been narrated from Ibn Abbas, from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), that he said: "*al-Darii'* is something in the Fire, resembling thorns, more bitter than aloes, more foul than carrion, and hotter than the Fire." [138] [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 20/30.]] The Prophet named it *darii'*. 

'Amr ibn 'Ubayd said: al-Hasan said nothing about *al-darii'* except that it is part of the punishment that Allah has concealed. Ibn Kaysan said: it is a food by which they become humbled and abased and beseech Allah, and according to this interpretation the meaning is "that which humbles" (al-mudarri').

Abu al-Darda' and al-Hasan said: Allah will disfigure the faces of the people of the Fire on the Day of Resurrection, making them resemble their evil deeds in the world, and He will beautify the faces of the people of Paradise, making them resemble their good deeds in the world. Allah will send hunger upon the people of the Fire until what they suffer is made light in comparison; they will call for help and be given *al-darii'*, and they will call for help and be given food of choking throat, recalling that they used to swallow morsels of choking food in the world with water; so they will ask for drink because of their thirst for a thousand years, and they will be given to drink from a boiling spring, neither wholesome nor pleasant. Whenever they bring it near their faces, it strips off the skin of their faces and roasts it; when it reaches their bellies, it cuts them up. This is His saying: ﴿And they are given boiling water to drink, and it cuts their bowels to pieces.﴾

The exegetes said: When this verse was revealed, the polytheists said: "Our camels will grow fat on *al-darii'*!" So Allah revealed: ﴿It neither fattens nor satisfies hunger.﴾ And it is said: camels graze on it while it is fresh; when it dries, nothing eats it, and its fresh form is called *al-shibraq*, not *al-darii'*.

﴿Faces, that Day, joyful,﴾ pleased with their striving in the world; ﴿well-pleased in the Hereafter,﴾ when they are given Paradise in return for their deeds, and rewarded for the reward of their striving in the Hereafter, well-pleased. ﴿In a lofty Garden,﴾ ﴿where they hear no idle talk.﴾ Idle talk is futility and falsehood; it was also said: a false oath. ﴿Therein is a flowing spring,﴾ ﴿therein are raised couches,﴾ ﴿and cups set out,﴾ ﴿and cushions arranged,﴾ ﴿and carpets spread out.﴾ *Namariq* means cushions, pillows and armrests set in rows, placed side by side; its singular is *namraqah*. The poet said:

*Elders and youths, handsome of face,*
*upon arranged couches and cushions.* [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 20/34.]]

﴿Zarabi (carpets)﴾ means broad rugs. Ibn Abbas said: they are fine cloths with a soft nap; the singular is *zaribah*. ﴿Spread out (mabthuthah)﴾: spread wide; it was also said: scattered throughout the gatherings.

﴿Will they not look...﴾ — the exegetes said: when Allah described what is in Paradise in this surah, the people of disbelief and error were astonished and denied it, so Allah reminded them of His creation, saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿Will they not look at the camels, how they were created?﴾

The camel was among the sustenance of the Arabs and those around them. The wise have spoken regarding why Allah singled out the camel from among all animals. Muqatil said: because they had never seen a beast greater than it, and few of them had seen the elephant. Al-Kalbi said: because it rises with its load while kneeling, and no other animal does so; nor is any animal as easy to lead or drive as it. Qatadah said: Allah mentioned the elevation of the couches of Paradise and their carpets, so they said: "How shall we ascend?" So Allah revealed this verse.

Al-Hasan was asked about this verse, and it was said to him: "Is the elephant not greater as a wonder?" He said: As for the elephant, the Arabs are far removed from it; moreover, it is a swine, which one does not ride, nor eat its flesh, nor milk its yield; whereas the camel is among the most precious and valued property of the Arabs.

Al-Hasan also said: they eat only the date-stone and fodder, and it yields milk. It was said: because in its size it is gentle to heavy loads and submits to a weak leader, so that a small child can take hold of its halter and lead it wherever he wishes.

Ustadh Abu al-Qasim ibn Habib related that he saw in some exegesis that a mouse took hold of a she-camel's halter and began pulling her, while the she-camel followed, until it entered the hole and pulled the halter; then the she-camel moved and pulled it back, bringing her mouth near the mouse's hole. Glory be to Him who measured it and subjected it.

Abdullah ibn Hamid informed us, saying: Ahmad ibn Abdullah informed us, saying: Muhammad ibn al-'Ala' related to us, saying:

Waki' related to us from Yunus ibn Abi Ishaq, from his father, from Shurayh, that he used to say: "Come out with us to al-Kunasah until we look at ﴿the camels, how they were created﴾."

It was said: "the camels" here means the clouds, but I have found no basis for this in the books of the imams. ﴿And at the sky, how it was raised,﴾ ﴿and at the mountains, how they were set up,﴾ ﴿and at the earth, how it was spread out (sutihat)﴾ — spread out.

Anas ibn Malik said: I prayed behind 'Ali ibn Abi Talib, and he recited ﴿Will you not look at the camels, how they were created, and so they were raised, and set up, and spread out﴾, with the ta' vowelled with a damma (on the verb "spread out": *sutihat*, with a raised ta').

And al-Hasan read *suttihat* with shaddah.

Abu Muhammad ibn al-Qasim informed me, saying: Isma'il ibn Majid related to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ibrahim ibn Sa'id related to us, saying: Sa'id ibn Hafs related to us, saying: I recited to Ma'qil ibn Abdullah, from Ikrimah ibn Khalid, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas, from Ubayy ibn Ka'b, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever recites Surat al-Ghashiyah, Allah will reckon with him with an easy reckoning." [137] [[Tafsir Majma' al-Bayan: 10/333.]]

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

﴿Has there come to you the report of the Overwhelming?﴾ That is, the Resurrection, which overwhelms everything; this is the view of most exegetes.

Sa'id ibn Jubayr and Muhammad ibn Ka'b said: "al-Ghashiyah" is the Fire. Their evidence is the Almighty's saying: ﴿And the Fire will cover their faces...﴾

﴿Faces, that Day,﴾ that is, the Day of Resurrection. It was said: ﴿in humiliation﴾, abased. ﴿Labouring, toiling,﴾ some said: that is, labouring in the Fire and toiling therein. Al-Hasan and Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: they did not work for Allah in the world, so they are made to labour and toil in the Fire, struggling with chains and shackles. This is also the narration of al-Awfi from Ibn Abbas. Qatadah said: they were disdainful of obedience in the world, so they are made to labour and toil in the Fire.

Al-Kalbi said: they are dragged on their faces in the Fire. Al-Dahhak said: they are commanded to climb a mountain of iron in the Fire. And al-Nasb means persistent labour.

Ikrimah and al-Suddi said: "labouring" in the world through sins, "toiling" in the Fire on the Day of Resurrection. Sa'id ibn Jubayr and Zayd ibn Aslam said: they are the monks and the dwellers of the hermitages. This is also the narration of Abu al-Duha from Ibn Abbas.

﴿Burning in a scorching Fire.﴾ Ibn Mas'ud said: they wade through the Fire as camels wade through mud.

The common reading is with a fatha on the ta'. Abu 'Amr, Ya'qub and Abu Bakr read it with a damma (tusla), in consideration of His saying: ﴿They will be given to drink from a boiling spring (ʿayn āniyah)﴾. Qatadah said: its cooking has been going on since Allah created the heavens and the earth.

﴿They will have no food except from *darii'*﴾. Muhammad, Ikrimah and Qatadah said: it is a thorny plant lying flat on the ground, which the people of the East call "firsh al-sharq"; when it dries out, they call it *al-darii'*, and it is the most wretched and foul food. This is also the narration of al-Awfi from Ibn Abbas. Al-Wali said from him: it is a tree of fire. Ibn Zayd said: in this world, *al-darii'* is dry thorn that has no leaves, which the Arabs call *al-darii'*; but in the Hereafter it is thorn of fire.

Al-Kalbi said: no animal approaches it when it dries, and nothing grazes on it. Sa'id ibn Jubayr said it is stones. Ata' related from Ibn Abbas: it is something cast up by the salt sea, which the people of Yemen call *al-darii'*.

It has been narrated from Ibn Abbas, from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), that he said: "*al-Darii'* is something in the Fire, resembling thorns, more bitter than aloes, more foul than carrion, and hotter than the Fire." [138] [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 20/30.]] The Prophet named it *darii'*. 

'Amr ibn 'Ubayd said: al-Hasan said nothing about *al-darii'* except that it is part of the punishment that Allah has concealed. Ibn Kaysan said: it is a food by which they become humbled and abased and beseech Allah, and according to this interpretation the meaning is "that which humbles" (al-mudarri').

Abu al-Darda' and al-Hasan said: Allah will disfigure the faces of the people of the Fire on the Day of Resurrection, making them resemble their evil deeds in the world, and He will beautify the faces of the people of Paradise, making them resemble their good deeds in the world. Allah will send hunger upon the people of the Fire until what they suffer is made light in comparison; they will call for help and be given *al-darii'*, and they will call for help and be given food of choking throat, recalling that they used to swallow morsels of choking food in the world with water; so they will ask for drink because of their thirst for a thousand years, and they will be given to drink from a boiling spring, neither wholesome nor pleasant. Whenever they bring it near their faces, it strips off the skin of their faces and roasts it; when it reaches their bellies, it cuts them up. This is His saying: ﴿And they are given boiling water to drink, and it cuts their bowels to pieces.﴾

The exegetes said: When this verse was revealed, the polytheists said: "Our camels will grow fat on *al-darii'*!" So Allah revealed: ﴿It neither fattens nor satisfies hunger.﴾ And it is said: camels graze on it while it is fresh; when it dries, nothing eats it, and its fresh form is called *al-shibraq*, not *al-darii'*.

﴿Faces, that Day, joyful,﴾ pleased with their striving in the world; ﴿well-pleased in the Hereafter,﴾ when they are given Paradise in return for their deeds, and rewarded for the reward of their striving in the Hereafter, well-pleased. ﴿In a lofty Garden,﴾ ﴿where they hear no idle talk.﴾ Idle talk is futility and falsehood; it was also said: a false oath. ﴿Therein is a flowing spring,﴾ ﴿therein are raised couches,﴾ ﴿and cups set out,﴾ ﴿and cushions arranged,﴾ ﴿and carpets spread out.﴾ *Namariq* means cushions, pillows and armrests set in rows, placed side by side; its singular is *namraqah*. The poet said:

*Elders and youths, handsome of face,*
*upon arranged couches and cushions.* [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 20/34.]]

﴿Zarabi (carpets)﴾ means broad rugs. Ibn Abbas said: they are fine cloths with a soft nap; the singular is *zaribah*. ﴿Spread out (mabthuthah)﴾: spread wide; it was also said: scattered throughout the gatherings.

﴿Will they not look...﴾ — the exegetes said: when Allah described what is in Paradise in this surah, the people of disbelief and error were astonished and denied it, so Allah reminded them of His creation, saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿Will they not look at the camels, how they were created?﴾

The camel was among the sustenance of the Arabs and those around them. The wise have spoken regarding why Allah singled out the camel from among all animals. Muqatil said: because they had never seen a beast greater than it, and few of them had seen the elephant. Al-Kalbi said: because it rises with its load while kneeling, and no other animal does so; nor is any animal as easy to lead or drive as it. Qatadah said: Allah mentioned the elevation of the couches of Paradise and their carpets, so they said: "How shall we ascend?" So Allah revealed this verse.

Al-Hasan was asked about this verse, and it was said to him: "Is the elephant not greater as a wonder?" He said: As for the elephant, the Arabs are far removed from it; moreover, it is a swine, which one does not ride, nor eat its flesh, nor milk its yield; whereas the camel is among the most precious and valued property of the Arabs.

Al-Hasan also said: they eat only the date-stone and fodder, and it yields milk. It was said: because in its size it is gentle to heavy loads and submits to a weak leader, so that a small child can take hold of its halter and lead it wherever he wishes.

Ustadh Abu al-Qasim ibn Habib related that he saw in some exegesis that a mouse took hold of a she-camel's halter and began pulling her, while the she-camel followed, until it entered the hole and pulled the halter; then the she-camel moved and pulled it back, bringing her mouth near the mouse's hole. Glory be to Him who measured it and subjected it.

Abdullah ibn Hamid informed us, saying: Ahmad ibn Abdullah informed us, saying: Muhammad ibn al-'Ala' related to us, saying:

Waki' related to us from Yunus ibn Abi Ishaq, from his father, from Shurayh, that he used to say: "Come out with us to al-Kunasah until we look at ﴿the camels, how they were created﴾."

It was said: "the camels" here means the clouds, but I have found no basis for this in the books of the imams. ﴿And at the sky, how it was raised,﴾ ﴿and at the mountains, how they were set up,﴾ ﴿and at the earth, how it was spread out (sutihat)﴾ — spread out.

Anas ibn Malik said: I prayed behind 'Ali ibn Abi Talib, and he recited ﴿Will you not look at the camels, how they were created, and so they were raised, and set up, and spread out﴾, with the ta' vowelled with a damma (on the verb "spread out": *sutihat*, with a raised ta').

And al-Hasan read *suttihat* with shaddah.

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 88, verses 21–26:

﴿So remind them. You are only a reminder. You are not over them a controller.﴾ That is, not a compeller or a forceful tyrant who makes them accept faith. Then that was abrogated by the verse of fighting. Harun read ﴿بِمُسِيْطَرٍ﴾ (with a fatha on the ṭāʾ), and this is the dialect of Tamim.

﴿Except for him who turns away and disbelieves.﴾ The scholars differed regarding the construction of this exception. Some of them said: it refers back to His saying ﴿so remind﴾. The sense of the verse is: "So remind your people, except for those among them who turn away and disbelieve, for reminding will not benefit them." It was also said that its meaning is: "You are not over them a controller, except over those who turn away and disbelieve, for you will fight them until they become Muslim." And it was said: it refers to what follows it, and its implied sense is: "But whoever turns away and disbelieves."

﴿Then Allah will punish him with the greatest punishment.﴾ This is the Fire. He said "the greatest" because they were punished in this world with hunger, drought, killing, and captivity. The evidence for this interpretation is the recitation of Ibn Mas'ud: "Except for him who turns away and disbelieves, then Allah will punish him with the greatest punishment."

﴿Indeed, to Us is their return.﴾ That is, their coming back and their final return. Abu Ja'far read ﴿إِيَابَهُمْ﴾ with a shaddah on the yāʾ. Abu Hatim said: this is not permissible, and if it were permissible here, it would be permissible in ﴿al-siyam﴾ and ﴿al-qiyam﴾ as well.

﴿Then indeed, upon Us is their reckoning.﴾

﴿Then Allah will punish him with the greatest punishment.﴾ This is the Fire. He said "the greatest" because they were punished in this world with hunger, drought, killing, and captivity. The evidence for this interpretation is the recitation of Ibn Mas'ud: "Except for him who turns away and disbelieves, then Allah will punish him with the greatest punishment."

﴿Indeed, to Us is their return.﴾ That is, their coming back and their final return. Abu Ja'far read ﴿إِيَابَهُمْ﴾ with a shaddah on the yāʾ. Abu Hatim said: this is not permissible, and if it were permissible here, it would be permissible in ﴿al-siyam﴾ and ﴿al-qiyam﴾ as well.

﴿Then indeed, upon Us is their reckoning.﴾
